agency: Alaska Department of Environmental Conservation, Water Division
credentials: Certified installer (18 AAC 72.405)
notes: DEC publishes a current certified installer list; the municipalities of Anchorage and Valdez run their own programs.

agency: Alabama Onsite Wastewater Board
credentials: Basic, Advanced I and Advanced II installer licenses; Pumper license; Manufacturer license
notes: Installer licenses carry bond requirements that rise with the license class. The board's search checks one name at a time.

agency: Arkansas Department of Health, Onsite Wastewater
credentials: Advanced septic installer license; Septic tank cleaner (truck) license; Certified monitoring personnel; Designated representative permit
notes: The Health Department licenses installers and septic tank cleaners separately; designated representatives perform site evaluations.

agency: Arizona Registrar of Contractors
credentials: CR-41 Septic Tanks and Systems (dual) contractor license
notes: Septic work in Arizona requires a contractor license in class CR-41; counties issue the permit for each system.

agency: Contractors State License Board (CSLB)
credentials: C-42 Sanitation System contractor license
notes: California has no license named for septic work; septic systems fall under the C-42 Sanitation System classification. Counties issue system permits.

agency: County health departments (rules set by CDPHE Regulation 43)
credentials: County systems installer or contractor license
notes: Colorado has no statewide septic installer license; each county licenses installers under the state's Regulation 43 standards.

agency: Connecticut Department of Public Health (licensing through the state eLicense system)
credentials: Subsurface sewage disposal system installer license; Subsurface sewage disposal system cleaner license
list_name: Connecticut State Licenses and Credentials open data
notes: Connecticut licenses septic installers and cleaners (pumpers) under Chapter 393a; active licenses are published daily on data.ct.gov.

agency: District of Columbia (no septic licensing program)
notes: Nearly all of the District is on public sewer.

agency: Delaware DNREC
credentials: Class E system contractor/installer license
list_name: DNREC Class E contractor roster (Delaware open data)
notes: Delaware publishes its Class E septic contractor roster as public-domain open data, including company phone and email.

agency: Florida Department of Environmental Protection, Operator Certification Program
credentials: Registered septic tank contractor; Master septic tank contractor; Certificate of authorization (business)
notes: Florida registers septic tank contractors under Chapter 489, Part III. State-certified plumbing contractors may also do septic work. The DEP search shows name, number, class and status only.

agency: Georgia Department of Public Health, Environmental Health
credentials: Certified septic tank installer (residential, commercial, drip and mound endorsements); Certified septic tank company; Pumper; Maintenance contractor
notes: Georgia certifies septic installers and companies through the Department of Public Health; county environmental health offices administer the exams and permits.

agency: Hawaii DCCA Contractors License Board
credentials: Contractor classes A, C-9, C-37, C-37a and C-43 (no septic-specific license)
notes: Hawaii has no license named for septic work; cesspool and septic jobs fall under general and plumbing-related contractor classes.

agency: County environmental health offices (567 IAC chapter 69)
credentials: County requirements
notes: Iowa sets septic rules statewide but leaves contractor requirements to counties.

agency: Idaho's seven public health districts, under Idaho DEQ rules
credentials: Standard/basic installer registration permit; Complex installer registration permit; Septic pumper permit
list_name: Public health district permitted installer and pumper lists
notes: Idaho installers and pumpers hold permits from the public health districts. Idaho Code 9-348 prohibits using the state's lists as a mailing or phone list.

agency: Illinois Department of Public Health, Private Sewage Disposal Program
credentials: Private sewage installation contractor license; Private sewage pumping contractor license
notes: Illinois licenses the individuals who install and pump private sewage (septic) systems; licenses are issued to people rather than companies.

agency: County health departments (rules set by the Indiana Department of Health)
credentials: County installer registration
notes: Indiana has no statewide septic installer license; counties register installers.

agency: County sanitary codes (KDHE sets minimum standards)
credentials: County licenses
notes: Kansas counties license septic installers. K.S.A. 45-230 restricts using public-record name lists for solicitation.

agency: Kentucky Cabinet for Health and Family Services, Installer Certification Program
credentials: Certified onsite sewage system installer
notes: Kentucky certifies septic installers, but has no online lookup; the program confirms certification by phone.

agency: Louisiana Department of Health, Onsite Wastewater Program
credentials: Basic installer; Combination installer; Maintenance provider
notes: The Louisiana Department of Health publishes its active installer list, which marks installers who can also maintain mechanical (aerobic) plants.

agency: Local boards of health (Title 5)
credentials: Town installer permits; State-certified Title 5 inspectors and soil evaluators
notes: Massachusetts towns permit septic installers; the state certifies Title 5 inspectors and soil evaluators.

agency: Maryland Department of the Environment
credentials: BAT (Best Available Technology) certified installer; County septic installer licenses in some counties
notes: Maryland certifies installers of nitrogen-reducing BAT septic units; installers also need the unit maker's certification, and some counties require a local license.

agency: Maine CDC, Subsurface Wastewater Program
credentials: Licensed site evaluator; Voluntary installer certification
notes: Maine licenses site evaluators who design systems; installer certification is voluntary.

agency: Michigan EGLE Septage Waste Program (pumpers); county health departments (installers)
credentials: Septage hauler license (Part 117)
notes: Michigan licenses septage haulers statewide; septic installers are licensed by county health departments, and Michigan has no statewide sanitary code.

agency: Minnesota Pollution Control Agency (SSTS program)
credentials: SSTS business license (installer, maintainer, service provider, designer, inspector); Individual SSTS certifications
notes: Minnesota licenses septic (SSTS) businesses and certifies the individuals who work for them. The MPCA search shows each business's license, insurance and bond status.

agency: Missouri DHSS Onsite Wastewater Treatment program
credentials: Registered basic installer; Registered advanced installer
notes: Missouri registers onsite system installers; no public download of the registry was found.

agency: Mississippi State Department of Health, On-Site Wastewater
credentials: Certified installer; Certified pumper/hauler; Certified maintenance provider
notes: Mississippi certifies septic installers, pumpers and maintenance providers through the State Department of Health.

agency: County health departments (Montana DEQ licenses septic pumpers)
credentials: County installer licenses; State septic pumper license
notes: Montana counties license installers; the state licenses pumpers.

agency: NC Onsite Wastewater Contractors & Inspectors Certification Board
credentials: Grade Level II installer; Grade Level IV installer; Point-of-sale inspector
notes: North Carolina certifies onsite wastewater installers by grade and certifies inspectors; the board publishes its certification list.

agency: North Dakota DEQ and local public health units
credentials: Annual septic installer license
list_name: ND annual active licensed installer list and local health unit lists
notes: North Dakota began licensing septic installers statewide under 2025 legislation (SB 2267); local public health units administer the program.

agency: Nebraska Department of Water, Energy, and Environment (Title 124)
credentials: Certified installer; Pumper; Inspector; Soil evaluator; Mound system
list_name: NDEE certified onsite wastewater professionals list
notes: Nebraska certifies onsite wastewater professionals by role: installers, pumpers, inspectors, soil evaluators and mound system installers.

agency: NH Department of Environmental Services, Subsurface Systems Bureau
credentials: Permitted installer (RSA 485-A:36); Permitted designer
list_name: NHDES permitted septic designer and installer list (October 2026)
notes: New Hampshire requires a NHDES permit to design or install a septic system; the Subsurface Systems Bureau publishes the list of permitted designers and installers.

agency: Local health departments
credentials: Local requirements
notes: New Jersey leaves septic installer requirements to local health departments.

agency: NMED Liquid Waste Program and the Construction Industries Division
credentials: CID MM-1, MM-98, MS-1 or MS-3 license; NMED installer specialist certification
notes: New Mexico septic installers need a Construction Industries Division license; homeowners may install their own systems under NMED rules.

agency: Nevada State Contractors Board; local health districts permit systems
credentials: C-27 individual sewerage contractor license
notes: Nevada septic work falls under the Contractors Board's C-27 sewerage classification; local health districts permit individual systems.

agency: County health departments (NYSDOH sets standards)
credentials: County licenses where required
notes: New York has no statewide septic installer license; some counties license installers.

agency: County health districts (OAC 3701-29)
credentials: County installer and service provider registration
notes: Ohio installers register with each county health district they work in.

agency: Oklahoma DEQ, Environmental Complaints and Local Services
credentials: Certified installer (subsurface, lagoon, aerobic spray, aerobic drip)
notes: Oklahoma certifies septic installers by system type: subsurface, lagoon, aerobic spray and aerobic drip.

agency: Oregon DEQ, Sewage Disposal Service licensing
credentials: Sewage disposal service license (installer, pumper); DEQ installer certification
notes: Oregon licenses sewage disposal businesses and certifies the installers who work for them.

agency: Local sewage enforcement officers (PA DEP Act 537 program)
credentials: DEP-recognized installer (course completion, not a license)
notes: Pennsylvania has no state septic installer license; local sewage enforcement officers permit each system. Our Pennsylvania listings come from the Pennsylvania Septage Management Association member directory.

agency: Rhode Island DEM, OWTS program
credentials: OWTS installer license (3-year, exam)
notes: Rhode Island licenses septic (OWTS) installers for three-year terms after an exam.

agency: South Carolina Department of Environmental Services
credentials: Tier 1, Tier 2 and Tier 3 installer licenses; Pumper/hauler license
notes: South Carolina licenses septic installers in three tiers and licenses pumpers; licenses renew yearly. State law (S.C. Code 30-2-50) bars using this data for commercial solicitation.

agency: South Dakota State Plumbing Commission
credentials: Individual and small on-site wastewater system installer license
list_name: Plumbing Commission small wastewater installer roster
notes: South Dakota licenses septic installers through the State Plumbing Commission.

agency: Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation, Division of Water Resources
credentials: Conventional installer permit; Alternative system permits (low-pressure pipe, mound, lagoon, aerobic); Pumper permit
notes: Tennessee permits septic installers yearly by system type; permits expire December 31.

agency: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ)
credentials: OSSF installer (Basic and Advanced); Site evaluator; Designated representative; Maintenance provider and maintenance technician
notes: TCEQ licenses the individuals who install, evaluate and maintain on-site sewage facilities (OSSF), including maintenance providers for aerobic systems.

agency: Utah DEQ Division of Water Quality
credentials: Level 1, 2 and 3 onsite professional certification
notes: Utah certifies onsite professionals who design, inspect and maintain systems; there is no separate installer license.

agency: Virginia DPOR, Board for Waterworks and Wastewater Works Operators and Onsite Sewage System Professionals
credentials: Conventional and alternative onsite sewage system installer (journeyman, master); Onsite sewage system operator; Onsite soil evaluator
notes: Virginia licenses septic installers, operators and soil evaluators at journeyman and master levels; DPOR updates its lists every five business days.

agency: Vermont DEC (voluntary installer certification); designers licensed by the Office of Professional Regulation
credentials: Voluntary installer certification; Licensed designers
notes: Vermont licenses septic designers; installer certification is voluntary.

agency: County health departments (designers licensed by the state)
credentials: County certified installer
notes: Washington counties certify septic installers; the state licenses designers.

agency: Wisconsin DSPS
credentials: Master plumber (installation); POWTS maintainer
notes: Wisconsin has no separate septic installer license; private onsite systems are installed under plumbing licenses and maintained by licensed POWTS maintainers.

agency: West Virginia Office of Environmental Health Services
credentials: Class I installer certification; Class II installer certification
notes: West Virginia certifies septic installers in two classes through the Office of Environmental Health Services.

agency: County health departments (Wyoming DEQ permits large systems)
credentials: County licenses
notes: Wyoming counties license septic installers; DEQ permits only systems of 2,000 gallons per day or more.
